result.coreDiagnosis: The candidate's profile exhibits significant job hopping with short tenures at Associate PM levels, raising immediate red flags for sustained ownership and technical depth required for a mid-level Product Manager (Technical) role.
result.roleFitVerdict: The profile presents as a high-velocity feature PM with strong metrics but lacks the sustained tenure and deep technical tradeoff judgment expected for a mid-level Product Manager (Technical) role.
recruiterScan: (Tenure) Significant job hopping: 4 roles in ~3.5 years (Oct 2020 - Present), with 3 roles under 6 months, indicating high instability.
(Level) Bulk of experience is at 'Associate Product Manager' level, suggesting a more junior scope than expected for a 3-5 year mid-level PMT.
(Technical Depth) AI/LLM buzzwords are present, but the technical contribution is described at an API usage level, not deep system design or technical tradeoff judgment.
(Impact) Strong metric-driven bullets, but the short tenures make 'end-to-end ownership' of a product area difficult to credit for sustained impact.
(Domain) Broad domain experience (SaaS, EdTech, E-commerce) lacks deep, sustained focus in a single technical product area.

topHiringRisks.title: Excessive Job Hopping & Tenure Instability
topHiringRisks.description: The candidate has held 4 roles in approximately 3.5 years, with three of those tenures being less than 6 months. This pattern raises significant concerns about commitment, ability to see projects through to long-term impact, and sustained growth in a single product area, which is critical for a mid-level PMT.

topHiringRisks.title: Insufficient Technical Depth for PMT
topHiringRisks.description: While AI/LLM terms are used, the resume primarily describes feature delivery and business impact. There's limited evidence of deep technical tradeoff discussions, influencing architecture, or earning engineer trust through technical fluency beyond using APIs, which is a core expectation for a Product Manager (Technical).

topHiringRisks.title: Level Mismatch & Lack of Sustained Ownership
topHiringRisks.description: The majority of the candidate's experience is at the 'Associate Product Manager' level, and the short tenures across roles make it difficult to ascertain sustained end-to-end product area ownership. The profile reads as a high-velocity feature PM, not a PM who has owned and grown a complex technical product area over multiple years, as expected for a mid-level PMT.

rewriteExample.before: Re-engineered the Raw Material Planner by restructuring end-to-end planning workflows, standardising data inputs, and eliminating process inefficiencies, cutting raw material wastage 14% and unlocking direct cost savings for production teams.
rewriteExample.after: Led the technical re-architecture of the Raw Material Planner, partnering with engineering to design a new data model and API integration layer that consolidated disparate inventory systems, reducing raw material wastage by 14% and directly cutting production costs by standardizing inputs and automating workflow validations.
rewriteExample.explanation: The original bullet described process improvements. The rewrite elevates the PM's role to leading a *technical re-architecture*, specifying *designing a new data model and API integration layer*. This demonstrates deeper technical involvement, understanding of system design, and partnership with engineering on the *how*, not just the *what*, which is crucial for a Product Manager (Technical) role. It also replaces generic 'eliminating process inefficiencies' with specific technical actions like 'automating workflow validations'.
